decisions.reason: Plugin A is the only crash: console stack pins SessionProgressBar's unconditional useSessionPendingInteraction call; alpha.2 contract removed that seat and added useSessionStatus while useSessions stays; plugin B uses no standard-kit hooks and throws nothing.

Cites dock-render-tree.md: one DrawerErrorBoundary wraps the whole input.dock list slot with null fallback, so A's render throw unmounts B's mounted sibling; button survives under the separate input.left boundary; quotes both the React follow-up and the host 'unmounted entries' log line.

Disable-A toggle read as necessary/sufficient causal evidence of render-crash coupling; explicit list of what it does not prove, including B's possible independent current-resolution bug; reinstalling B can never help because B was never broken; colleague theory refuted on five grounds.

Corrected code selects the hook by capability, reads pendingInteraction via useSessionStatus with optional chaining, and has a total degraded branch rendering the strip without pending state; silent degradation justified because a throw unmounts co-tenants — missing indicator cosmetic vs multi-plugin outage; legacy hook also guarded.

Client-half fix needing only hard refresh, no host restart; acceptance matrix asserts both entries co-mounted and B's paste/remove/re-paste flow with A enabled; hygiene: feature-detect kit seats, tenant's own boundary wrapper, host per-entry boundaries with isolation/atomicity/diagnosability trade-offs.

caps.reason: Final remedy migrates plugin A's component; B is identified as the innocent victim and the colleague's fix-both-registrations remedy is explicitly rejected.
